definition: The infrastructure and processes involved in deploying a trained model so it can respond to real-world inference requests, typically via an API.
details: Model serving systems handle concerns like batching, load balancing, autoscaling, and hardware utilization to serve models reliably and cost-effectively at scale.

explainer.lead: The infrastructure and processes that deploy a trained model so it can answer real-world inference requests, typically via an API. It handles batching, load balancing, autoscaling, and hardware utilization to serve reliably and cost-effectively at scale.

tiers.eli5: Like a restaurant kitchen set up to take orders and plate dishes quickly, even when the dining room suddenly fills up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set up batching, autoscaling, and load balancing so models meet latency targets without wasting hardware. A pitfall is ignoring batching or scaling limits, which causes slow responses or idle expensive GPUs.
tiers.paperLevel: Serving infrastructure receives inference requests, groups them into batches, balances load, and scales hardware to meet latency and throughput targets; throughput and latency trade off against each other.

explainer.example: An image classifier is served behind an API that batches incoming requests and adds replicas when traffic spikes.
